facts.claim: Arabic 114:1-6 = Tanzil Uthmani strings (ayat[]); CC BY 3.0, verbatim, credit Tanzil Project + link; byte-check vs tanzil.net on PC required
Hindi = saral bhaavarth from accepted translations (Tanzil hi.hindi/Suhel Farooq Khan, Muhammad Farooq Khan, Mahmud al-Hasan PD); nothing copied
Latin transliteration per ayah for the Devanagari ucharan (Tanzil ara-quran-la + quran411 ara-quran-la1)
Surah 114 = An-Nas (الناس), 'Mankind / The People'; last (114th) surah of the mushaf; 6 ayat; juz 30
An-Nas and al-Falaq together = 'Mu'awwidhatayn' (surahs of seeking refuge); An-Nas is the second

Makki/Madani: IKHTILAAF, no majority claimed. Makki: Qurtubi first view, Tanzil metadata 'meccan'. Madani: Ibn Kathir (AR 'wa huma madaniyyatan'), Qurtubi second view (Ibn Abbas one report, Qatada). Tabari, Ma'ariful, Ibn Kathir EN/Qurtubi 114 pages: no verdict
Order of revelation number: not in any opened source
Other name: only 'Mu'awwidhatayn' (shared). No separate name for 114 alone

Main message: seek refuge in Allah - Rabb, Malik and Ilah of mankind - from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws (whispers in people's hearts, from jinn and men). Ma'ariful: Nas = inner/hereafter side vs Falaq = worldly

SHAN-E-NUZUL: none of the opened 114 pages (Ibn Kathir EN, Qurtubi, Tabari, Ma'ariful) states a sahih-grade occasion for An-Nas. The sihr (Labid) report (Bukhari 5763) is an event; it does not say the surahs came down for it; 11-knots/11-ayat link unsound (Ibn Kathir nakarah, see 004). = NO sahih shan-e-nuzul. Only sahih context: Muslim 814 - verses sent down 'tonight' unlike any seen (Z1)
facts.grade: ikhtilaaf / pata nahi - not as fact

facts.claim: Safe script line: 'इस सूरह के उतरने की कोई सहीह-दर्जे की ख़ास वजह नहीं मिलती' + P3 makki/madani ikhtilaaf line; optionally Z1 as the only sahih context. No sihr story, no scene

SAHIH: 'Uqba bin 'Amir - the Prophet SAW said (in wonder) verses were sent down tonight the like of which was never seen: Qul a'udhu bi rabbil-falaq and Qul a'udhu bi rabbin-nas. Muslim 814 (Tirmidhi: hasan sahih, per Qurtubi). Report only, no ruling
SAHIH (report only): 'A'isha - every night at bed the Prophet SAW joined palms, blew, recited Ikhlas, Falaq, Nas and wiped his body, 3 times. Bukhari 5017 (also 5748)
SAHIH (report only): 'A'isha - in illness the Prophet SAW recited the Mu'awwidhat over himself; in his last illness she recited and wiped his hands over him. Bukhari 5016 (optional)

114:1-3 - Qul a'udhu: say / I seek refuge; Rabb = owner, nurturer of everything; Malik = King, sovereign over everything (some people are kings and claim rule); Ilah = the one worshipped (some people worship others). Three attributes: refuge is sought only in Him, not in kings or the powerful (Qurtubi; Ibn Kathir: 'Lord of everything, King of everything, God of everything'; Tabari; Ma'ariful on Rabb)

114:4 - al-waswas = the whisperer (Shaytan; whisper = suggestion to the heart); al-khannas = the one who withdraws when Allah is remembered (Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada; Ibn Kathir, Tabari). Ibn Abbas: whispers when the person is heedless, withdraws when he remembers Allah. Tabari: not limited to one form (urges sin / discourages obedience)
114:5 - yuwaswisu fi suduri an-nas: whispers into people's hearts/chests (Tabari: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada; Ibn Kathir)

114:6 - min al-jinnati wa an-nas: the whisperers are of jinn and of men - core agreed (Ibn Kathir citing Ibn Jarir and 6:112; Tabari: Ibn Zayd; Qurtubi). Detail ikhtilaaf (whether 'nas' includes jinn; Ibn Zayd: human whisperers worse because visible) - video keeps only the core

Whole surah order: Rabb -> Malik -> Ilah (general to specific, Qurtubi) then the evil of the whisperer; Ma'ariful: Falaq seeks refuge from worldly hardships, Nas from trials of the hereafter; Ibn Kathir: 'The only person who is safe is He Whom Allah protects'
